title: Find the right office: Which authority is responsible for my town?
desc: Choose state, district and town – go to the official office finder: Ausländerbehörde, Bürgeramt, Jobcenter, Finanzamt, Amtsgericht. Free, in 13 languages.
h1: Find the right office: State → District → Town
intro: Choose where you live. You get the official name of your town (Gemeinde) and your district (Kreis) and the official search portals that tell you which authority is responsible, with its address.
why: Which authority is responsible depends on where you live: some tasks are done by the town or city (Gemeinde, Stadt), others by the district (Kreis), others by a state or federal authority. This is a little different in every federal state (Bundesland). That is why we do not give you guessed addresses. We take you to the official search portals.

stepsTitle: How to find the right office
steps: Above, choose federal state, district and town – or type the name of your town.

Open the service portal of your federal state. Enter your town and your request there, for example „Aufenthaltstitel verlängern“ (extend residence permit), „Wohnsitz anmelden“ (register your address) or „Wohngeld“ (housing benefit).
Put the address in your letter
The portal tells you the responsible office with its address. Copy it into one of our letter templates.
Ask your town or city administration. In many regions, the public service number 115 can also help.
faq: What is the Amtlicher Gemeindeschlüssel (official municipality key)?

An 8-digit number that clearly identifies every town (Gemeinde) in Germany. The first 2 digits stand for the federal state, the next 3 for the administrative region and the district, the last 3 for the town.
Why does this page not show the address of the authority directly?

Responsibilities and addresses change and are different in each federal state. The service portals of the federal government and the states are kept up to date by the administration itself. That is why they are the safe source.
